note: Original draft content written from general knowledge, unreviewed. Nothing was copied from a course, book, phrasebook or website. Pointing, transliteration (capitals mark the stressed syllable), register labels and gender forms have NOT been checked by a native speaker. No audio exists for any item. Nothing here was tested with learners.

fillers.en: come on, let's go, okay then
fillers.usage: Urging, agreeing to go, or closing a conversation ('yalla bye').
fillers.note: From Arabic. Very common. Said sharply it can sound impatient.
fillers.confidenceReason: Meaning solid; stress is our best understanding.

fillers.usage: Agreeing or saying something is fine.
fillers.note: From Arabic. Keep it for friends and relaxed settings.

fillers.usage: Nudging someone to continue or hurry; can also express impatience.
fillers.note: Of Yiddish origin. Tone matters: it can be friendly or impatient.

fillers.usage: Friendly address to a man you are familiar with. Often used between men; avoid with older strangers and in formal settings.
fillers.genderNote: Said to a man. Do not use it for a woman unless you know the local custom.
fillers.note: The feminine counterpart achoti ('my sister') exists but we are less sure how it is used, so it is not taught here.

fillers.usage: Agreeing, accepting, saying you are fine. Safe in any setting.
fillers.note: Literally 'in order'.

fillers.usage: Describing a messy room, situation or schedule.
fillers.note: Used for a mess, not for pain or illness.

fillers.en: specifically, of all things, as it happens
fillers.usage: Pointing out that something is the opposite of what you expect, or exactly that one.
fillers.note: Hard to translate; the nuance depends on context. Learn it by example.
fillers.confidenceReason: Meaning is solid; the full range of use is subtle.

fillers.usage: 'Already' in time. Also said with a push, as in 'enough already'.
fillers.note: The impatient 'kvar!' use depends on tone; use it only with people you know.

fillers.en: no way, what do you mean, of course not
fillers.usage: Rejecting a suggestion or an accusation.
fillers.note: Literally 'what suddenly?'. Can sound sharp; use with friends.

fillers.usage: Reacting with surprise or confirming something.
fillers.note: From Arabic. The first letters are pronounced 'v', not 'w'.

fillers.usage: Praising a thing or a person. The literal meaning is a pity about the time (it is a waste).
fillers.note: Slang; do not translate word by word.

fillers.usage: Saying something is good. Some speakers may find it a little dated: we have not checked.
fillers.note: Meaning is clear; how current it sounds is not checked.
fillers.confidenceReason: Meaning is solid; frequency among younger speakers is unknown.

fillers.usage: Praising, agreeing, closing a thought. Fits most settings.
fillers.note: Means 'beauty'.

fillers.usage: Intensifying: really good, really tired.
fillers.note: Safe in most settings.

fillers.usage: Saying something is fun or pleasant.
fillers.note: Eize before a noun adds 'what a ...' to an exclamation.

fillers.usage: Asking someone to wait or pausing yourself.
fillers.note: Literally 'a moment'.

fillers.en: just because, for no reason, nothing special
fillers.usage: Answering 'why?' or 'what's up?' lightly.
fillers.note: Also used to mean 'for no reason'.

fillers.usage: Agreeing strongly.
fillers.note: Literally 'clear'.

fillers.usage: Getting to the point.
fillers.note: Of Yiddish origin. We are less sure of all the ways it is used.
fillers.confidenceReason: Meaning is solid; range of use is not checked.

fillers.usage: Saying something is simple or just so.
fillers.note: Also an adjective meaning 'simple'.

fillers.usage: Calling a group of friends together. Spelled the same as 'a female friend' (chavera) but pronounced differently.
fillers.note: Not to be confused with chavera, 'a female friend', written the same.
fillers.confidenceReason: Meaning is solid; the difference between the two readings depends on context.

fillers.usage: Stopping something.
fillers.note: Can be sharp if said with force. Safe with a smile and toda.
